subject: Discovery recap: reliability, graceful degradation, and SLOs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Price <samantha.price@finovate.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-01T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: reliability, graceful degradation, and SLOs

Hi Samantha — great to meet earlier today, thanks for the time. Per our discussion, I wanted to summarize the key pain points, success criteria, and proposed next steps so we have everything in one place. Please flag anything I missed or that you'd like reworded.

Pain points we heard
- Recent incidents impacting customer-facing availability and latency (see incident summary attached).
- Limited automated fallback behavior today — manual model/region failovers resulting in longer recovery time.
- Cost/quality tradeoffs: teams are hesitant to use cheaper fallbacks due to quality degradation concerns.

Incident highlights (from our convo) — please confirm
- Nov 2025: regional failover during a cloud networking incident; ~4 hours degraded service while manual routing was applied.
- Dec 2025: peak traffic event causing a 25–30% spike in P95 latency and increased error rates for short windows.

Current stack (your description)
- Mixed: primary calls to OpenAI (hosted) for high-quality responses + self-hosted Llama-serving cluster in GCP for cached/low-cost paths.
- Keys managed in on-prem HSM; data residency constrained to us-east for regulated workloads.

Primary goals / success criteria
1) Availability: target 99.9% or better for customer-facing inference endpoints.
2) Latency: P95 < 200ms for baseline flows, with graceful degradation paths that keep user flows acceptable.
3) Recovery: automated failover/recovery with RTO < 5 minutes for most failure classes.
4) Quality guardrails: fallback models or regions must remain within an acceptable quality delta (<= 2% on your key prompts/evals).

Suggested next steps
- I attached a short incident summary you mentioned and our Redwood SLA brief for initial context.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive (1 hour) with your infra/eng lead + our Solutions Engineer (Jonas) to review: incident root causes, routing policies, fallback model options, and PoC plan.
- Proposed PoC: 4-week sandbox on Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) with configured fallback policies (model variant + region routing) and instrumentation for the success criteria above. We can scope SLO targets and success metrics during the deep-dive.

Possible time slots next week for the deep-dive: Tue 3/3 10:00–11:00 PT, Wed 3/4 9:00–10:00 PT, Thu 3/5 1:00–2:00 PT. Do any of these work?

Outstanding questions for you (quick)
- Can you confirm the exact RTO/RPO constraints from your ops/incident runbook?
- Are there any strictly blocked regions beyond us-east for data residency?
- Do you have a short list of 6–8 fallback prompts we should use for quality regression checks?

Attachments: prod-incident-summary-2025Q4.pdf, redwood-sla-brief.pdf

Thanks again — happy to iterate on the PoC scope once we align on success metrics.

—Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
https://www.redwood.ai
From: Samantha Price <samantha.price@finovate.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-01T16:14:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: reliability, graceful degradation, and SLOs

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap, this matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

Incident confirmation
- Nov 2025: yes, that was a networking failover in our primary provider region — took ~4 hours to fully restore due to manual DNS and routing steps.
- Dec 2025: peak holiday traffic caused a latency spike (P95 to ~450ms) on our inference tier for ~20 minutes.

Constraints / environment notes
- Data residency: for regulated customer flows we must keep inference and logs in us-east for now. Non-sensitive traffic can be routed outside us-east.
- KMS/HSM: we keep keys in an on-prem HSM; any integration must support customer-managed keys.
- Peak throughput: typical bursts up to ~150 req/sec; sustained baseline closer to 40–60 req/sec.

Success criteria & budget
- The RTO target is aggressive but important: < 5 minutes for most automated recoveries. Manual backstops allowed for edge cases.
- Budget: we have an initial POC budget scoped at low-to-mid 5-figures; we need a clear ROI case tied to reduced downtime and improved latency.

For the deep-dive
- Wed 3/4 9:00–10:00 PT works for our engineering lead. Could Jonas lead the infra routing/fallback section? Also please include an example set of fallback models and estimated costs for the PoC.

I'll send the short list of fallback prompts and the runbook excerpt for RTO by EOD tomorrow.

—Samantha
Director of Engineering, Finovate AI
samantha.price@finovate.ai | +1 (617) 555-0143
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Price <samantha.price@finovate.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-02T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: reliability, graceful degradation, and SLOs

Thanks Samantha — great, Wed 3/4 9:00 PT is locked on our side. Jonas will cover routing/fallback design and I’ll own the PoC scope/cost estimates.

Quick responses to your asks:
- Fallback model examples: we typically propose a small-parameter quantized model (e.g., Llama-2-7B-quant) as an immediate low-cost fallback plus a distilled supervised variant for higher-quality degraded responses. For latency-critical microflows we can also route to a specialized smaller model with pre-warmed KV caches. I’ll bring estimated token/unit costs for each option to the deep-dive.
- Data residency & CMK: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) and private deployments (VPC/on-prem) — I attached our short SLA/architecture brief for reference.
- PoC scope (draft agenda): 1) review incident timeline and root causes, 2) routing/fallback policy design, 3) autoscaling and pre-warming, 4) PoC success metrics & instrumentation, 5) security/compliance checklist.

I’ve added our HubSpot record here for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/contact/87654321.

See you Wed — I’ll send a calendar invite with the agenda and attach the SLA brief.

—Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: reliability, graceful degradation, and SLOs

Hi Samantha — Jonas here (Solutions Eng). Quick note before Wed’s deep-dive: please include whoever owns your routing/DNS playbooks and your SLO doc if possible — it will help us map Redwood's fallback automation to your ops runbook.

On the fallback models: I’ll bring cost/latency benchmarks for a few quantized variants and a sample canary rollout policy that fails over by region or model depending on detected error classes.

Proposed addition to agenda: short review of your post-incident RCA (5–10 min) so we can align failure classes to automated responses.

Thanks — I’ll send meeting invite shortly and include dial-in + Zoom.

—Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
